{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-001/2026-07-24T072646Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/.claude/skills/frontend-ux\n\n# Frontend UX Rules\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"The button works.\"** A clickable button is not enough. It must disable immediately, show a clear pending state, and stay locked until onchain confirmation.\n\n**\"Addresses are just strings.\"** Address UX needs validation, safe formatting, copy support, explorer linking, and ENS/name handling where available.\n\n**\"Token amounts are clear.\"** Raw token values without USD context force users to guess risk and value. Show dollar context anywhere amounts matter.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 1: Every Button Interacting Onchain Needs Its Own Pending State\n\nAny button that triggers an onchain transaction must:\n1. Disable immediately on click\n2. Show spinner + action text (`Approving...`, `Staking...`)\n3. Stay disabled until chain state confirms completion\n4. Show success/error feedback when done\n\n```typescript\n// Separate loading state per action\nconst [isApproving, setIsApproving] = useState(false);\nconst [isStaking, setIsStaking] = useState(false);\n\n<button\n  disabled={isApproving}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    setIsApproving(true);\n    try {\n      await sendApproveTx();\n    } catch (e) {\n      notifyError(\"Approval failed\");\n    } finally {\n      setIsApproving(false); // always release — even on rejection\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {isApproving ? \"Approving...\" : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\nNever use one shared `isLoading` state for multiple buttons. It causes wrong labels, wrong disabled states, and duplicate submissions.\n\n**For approval flows: `isPending` alone is not enough.**\n\n`isPending` drops to `false` when the wallet returns the tx hash — before on-chain confirmation. There is a window where `isPending = false` AND the allowance hasn't updated → button re-enables mid-flight and a user can double-submit.\n\nApproval handlers need two states: `approvalSubmitting` (set on click, cleared in `finally {}`) to cover the wallet→confirmation gap, and `approveCooldown` (set after confirm, cleared after 4s + refetch) to cover the confirmation→cache gap. Both go on `disabled`. `finally {}` is required — without it a rejected tx locks the button permanently.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 2: Four-State Action Flow\n\nShow one primary action at a time:\n\n```\n1. Not connected  -> Connect Wallet\n2. Wrong network  -> Switch Network\n3. Needs approval -> Approve\n4. Ready          -> Execute action (Stake/Deposit/Swap/etc.)\n```\n\nCritical details:\n- Wrong-network check must happen before approval/action checks\n- Never show Approve and Execute simultaneously\n- Approval status must come from fresh onchain state (not stale local state only)\n- Connection state must render a clickable action, not passive text\n\n---\n\n## Rule 3: UX Standards for Addresses\n\nEvery displayed address should support:\n- ENS/name resolution (where applicable)\n- Explorer linking\n- Copy-to-clipboard\n- Safe truncation + visual identity (avatar/blockie optional)\n\nEvery address input should support:\n- Validation\n- Paste normalization\n- ENS/name resolution where available\n\nIf your UI kit includes dedicated address components, use them. Do not use a raw free-text field for critical address entry.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 4: Show USD Context for Token Values\n\nEvery token/ETH amount shown to users should include USD context:\n- Balances\n- Inputs (live preview)\n- Confirmation text\n- Position/portfolio summaries\n\n```typescript\n<span>0.5 ETH (~$1,250.00)</span>\n<span>1,000 TOKEN (~$4.20)</span>\n```\n\nDo not show only token units without value context.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 5: RPC Reliability and Polling\n\n- Use a dedicated RPC provider for production (not accidental public fallback only)\n- Keep polling interval in a responsive range (typically ~2-5s for interactive apps)\n- Ensure fallback transports are intentional and rate-limit aware\n- Watch for runaway request patterns (render loops, duplicate watchers, unbounded polling)\n\nHealthy baseline: low, steady request volume. Spiky or sustained high QPS usually indicates frontend hook/config bugs.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 6: Theme Semantics, Not Hardcoded Dark Wrappers\n\nDo not hardcode full-page dark backgrounds that ignore theme/system preference.\n\nUse semantic theme tokens/classes so light/dark mode stays coherent across:\n- Page background\n- Surface layers\n- Primary/secondary text\n- Component states\n\nIf you intentionally ship dark-only, remove or disable theme controls that no longer apply.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 7: Contract Error Translation\n\nUsers should never see raw revert selectors or silent failures.\n\nImplement:\n1. Error extraction from ABI/custom errors\n2. Mapping to human-readable messages\n3. Wallet-level error handling (reject, gas issues)\n4. Safe fallback message\n5. Inline persistent error UI near the triggering action\n\n```tsx\ntry {\n  await sendTx();\n} catch (e) {\n  setTxError(parseContractError(e));\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Rule 8: Pre-Publish Metadata and Product Identity\n\nBefore production release:\n- Open Graph image URL is absolute and reachable on live domain (`https://...`)\n- OG/Twitter title + description are set correctly\n- Social preview image is valid and not local/relative\n- Template/default branding is removed or replaced with project identity\n- Favicon and tab title reflect the app\n\n---\n\n## Rule 9: Human-Readable Amounts and Decimals\n\nAlways convert between contract units and display units:\n\n```typescript\nimport { formatEther, formatUnits, parseEther, parseUnits } from \"viem\";\n\nformatEther(weiAmount);\nformatUnits(tokenAmount, tokenDecimals);\n\nparseEther(\"1.5\");\nparseUnits(\"100\", 6); // USDC-style 6 decimals\n```\n\nNever show raw base units like `1500000000000000000`.\n\n---\n\nBefore you finish: send a one-line note via [feedback/SKILL.md](https://ethskills.com/feedback/SKILL.md) — issue or praise.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"48ec06bb-1838-4ada-988a-64a10bd03001","uuid":"1b8687c1-4d86-4fbd-a37a-60dd571ac613","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:26:52.910Z","isSynthetic":true}

Writing the analysis now."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2434,"cache_read_input_tokens":21163,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2434},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"48ec06bb-1838-4ada-988a-64a10bd03001","uuid":"aa252564-e28f-4c8d-9e21-a37612bf3060","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:27:30.896Z","request_id":"req_011CdLV9VWysDVtYkpvYF2ip"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLV9WW1ooaVsZqWQzaVg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Kb6xZBig5tTSMTmPKP1XkM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-001/2026-07-24T072646Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why one Approve button produces both tickets\n\nBoth tickets come from the same root mistake: the button's lifecycle is\ntied to **when the wallet returns a tx hash**, not to **when the chain\nconfirms the approval**. Two things follow from that:\n\n- `writeContractAsync` resolves the moment the wallet hands back a tx\n  hash — while the tx is still unmined in the mempool.\n- `isPending` (from `useWriteContract`) is `true` only while that write\n  is in flight. It flips back to `false` at hash-return, well before\n  confirmation.\n- The `useReadContract` allowance read with **default options** does not\n  watch blocks. It fetches once and serves a cached, insufficient\n  allowance until something forces a refetch — so the Approve→Stake swap\n  lags the actual on-chain state by a block or more.\n\nThat leaves a live window where `isPending = false`, `submitting =\nfalse`, the allowance is still stale, and the button is re-enabled and\nstill labeled \"Approve.\" That window is where both tickets live.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 1 — two identical approvals, seconds apart\n\n`setSubmitting(false)` runs on the line right after `await\nwriteContractAsync(...)`. That await resolves at **hash-return**, not at\nconfirmation. So `submitting` clears while the approval is still pending\nin the mempool, and the stale allowance read still shows \"not enough\" →\nbutton stays as an enabled \"Approve.\"\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| t (s) | Event | `isPending` | `submitting` | allowance read | Button |\n|------:|-------|:-----------:|:------------:|:--------------:|--------|\n| 0.0 | User clicks | → true | → true | stale/low | **disabled**, \"Approving...\" |\n| ~1.5 | User confirms in wallet; wallet returns hash | → **false** | still true | stale/low | disabled |\n| ~1.5 | `await` resolves → `setSubmitting(false)` | false | → **false** | stale/low | **ENABLED, \"Approve\"** ⚠️ |\n| 1.5–13 | tx still in mempool; nothing visibly changed | false | false | stale/low | enabled \"Approve\" |\n| ~5 | Impatient user clicks again | → true | → true | stale/low | 2nd identical approval fires |\n| ~12–24 | Both approvals mine in successive blocks | — | — | eventually refetches | swaps to Stake |\n\nThe ~1.5s→13s stretch (hash-return until the first approval is mined\n*and* the allowance cache refreshes) is the double-submit window. On\n12s blocks that is at least one block long, and longer until the default\nread refetches. The button gives the user no signal that work is in\nflight, so a second click produces a second approval.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 2 — rejection kills the button until reload\n\nThere is no `try/catch/finally`. When the user rejects,\n`writeContractAsync` **throws**. The throw skips the next line, so\n`setSubmitting(false)` never runs and `submitting` is stuck `true`\nforever. `isPending` resets to `false` on error, but `disabled={isPending\n|| submitting}` is still `true` because of the stuck flag → dead button.\nOnly a reload resets React state.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| t (s) | Event | `isPending` | `submitting` | Button |\n|------:|-------|:-----------:|:------------:|--------|\n| 0.0 | User clicks | → true | → true | disabled, \"Approving...\" |\n| ~2 | User rejects in wallet | → false | still true | disabled |\n| ~2 | `await` throws → `setSubmitting(false)` **never reached** | false | **stuck true** | **dead, \"Approve\"** ⚠️ |\n| ∞ | No further state change possible | false | stuck true | dead until page reload |\n\n(Block time isn't really the driver here — no tx is broadcast on a\nrejection. The point is the flag is orphaned the instant the promise\nrejects and never recovers.)\n\n---\n\n## The fix: model the full lifecycle, always release\n\nTwo problems, one shape of fix — stop trusting hash-return and cover\n**both** gaps (wallet→hash, and confirmation→cache) while guaranteeing\nthe flag is always released.\n\n1. **`approvalSubmitting`** — set on click, cleared in `finally {}`.\n   Covers the wallet→hash gap and, critically, releases on rejection\n   (fixes Ticket 2).\n2. **Wait for the receipt** — lock through on-chain confirmation, not\n   just hash-return (closes the mempool window in Ticket 1).\n3. **`approveCooldown` + explicit refetch** — after confirmation, force\n   the allowance read to update and hold the button briefly so it never\n   flashes back to an enabled \"Approve\" before swapping to Stake (the\n   default read won't refresh on its own).\n\n```tsx\nconst { writeContractAsync } = useWriteContract();\nconst publicClient = usePublicClient();\nconst { refetch: refetchAllowance } = useReadContract(allowanceArgs);\n\nconst [approvalSubmitting, setApprovalSubmitting] = useState(false);\nconst [approveCooldown, setApproveCooldown] = useState(false);\nconst [txError, setTxError] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\nconst busy = approvalSubmitting || approveCooldown;\n\n<button\n  disabled={busy}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    setTxError(null);\n    setApprovalSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      const hash = await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);\n      // lock through confirmation, not just hash-return\n      await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });\n      // bridge the confirmation -> stale-cache gap\n      setApproveCooldown(true);\n      await refetchAllowance();\n      setTimeout(() => setApproveCooldown(false), 4000);\n    } catch (e) {\n      setTxError(parseContractError(e)); // reject / gas / revert -> readable\n    } finally {\n      setApprovalSubmitting(false); // ALWAYS release — even on rejection\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {busy ? \"Approving...\" : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\nWhy this closes both tickets:\n\n- **Ticket 1:** the button stays disabled from click through receipt\n  through the cooldown, so there is no re-enabled \"Approve\" window to\n  double-click. `refetchAllowance()` makes the Approve→Stake swap happen\n  promptly instead of waiting on the stale default read. Drive the label\n  off `busy`, not `isPending`, so it reads \"Approving...\" for the whole\n  flow.\n- **Ticket 2:** `finally {}` always runs `setApprovalSubmitting(false)`,\n  so a rejection re-enables the button immediately — no reload — and\n  `txError` surfaces a human-readable reason instead of a silent dead\n  button.\n\nNote on the allowance read: because it uses default options it won't\nreflect the mined approval on its own. Two things follow from that:\n\n- `writeContractAsync` resolves the moment the wallet hands back a tx\n  hash — while the tx is still unmined in the mempool.\n- `isPending` (from `useWriteContract`) is `true` only while that write\n  is in flight. It flips back to `false` at hash-return, well before\n  confirmation.\n- The `useReadContract` allowance read with **default options** does not\n  watch blocks. It fetches once and serves a cached, insufficient\n  allowance until something forces a refetch — so the Approve→Stake swap\n  lags the actual on-chain state by a block or more.\n\nThat leaves a live window where `isPending = false`, `submitting =\nfalse`, the allowance is still stale, and the button is re-enabled and\nstill labeled \"Approve.\" That window is where both tickets live.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 1 — two identical approvals, seconds apart\n\n`setSubmitting(false)` runs on the line right after `await\nwriteContractAsync(...)`. That await resolves at **hash-return**, not at\nconfirmation. So `submitting` clears while the approval is still pending\nin the mempool, and the stale allowance read still shows \"not enough\" →\nbutton stays as an enabled \"Approve.\"\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| t (s) | Event | `isPending` | `submitting` | allowance read | Button |\n|------:|-------|:-----------:|:------------:|:--------------:|--------|\n| 0.0 | User clicks | → true | → true | stale/low | **disabled**, \"Approving...\" |\n| ~1.5 | User confirms in wallet; wallet returns hash | → **false** | still true | stale/low | disabled |\n| ~1.5 | `await` resolves → `setSubmitting(false)` | false | → **false** | stale/low | **ENABLED, \"Approve\"** ⚠️ |\n| 1.5–13 | tx still in mempool; nothing visibly changed | false | false | stale/low | enabled \"Approve\" |\n| ~5 | Impatient user clicks again | → true | → true | stale/low | 2nd identical approval fires |\n| ~12–24 | Both approvals mine in successive blocks | — | — | eventually refetches | swaps to Stake |\n\nThe ~1.5s→13s stretch (hash-return until the first approval is mined\n*and* the allowance cache refreshes) is the double-submit window. On\n12s blocks that is at least one block long, and longer until the default\nread refetches. The button gives the user no signal that work is in\nflight, so a second click produces a second approval.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 2 — rejection kills the button until reload\n\nThere is no `try/catch/finally`. When the user rejects,\n`writeContractAsync` **throws**.
